lines.text: Back to our story. A passing robot blocks the view while ours drives on, to one meter from the tag.
Photo three comes from one meter. Sigma is just one point five centimeters, so its noise is zero point zero zero zero two two eight.
Our variance plus drift is zero point zero zero one zero two one, so K is zero point eight two. From two meters, only zero point three three.
The guess jumps to two point nine nine seven, zero point five nine seven: about four millimeters from the true tag. Three good photos: locked.
Over a whole approach, the gain falls as photos pile up, to about zero point zero five, then climbs as photos sharpen near the tag.
The little drift we add with every photo keeps the gain above zero, so the filter never stops listening.
Before voting, a photo must pass some rules: no farther than three point five meters, no older than a quarter second.
Ambiguity at most zero point three: zero is sure, one is a coin flip. Skipped photos still go in the log.
No jump: the square root of dx squared plus dy squared must stay within zero point two five meters. Three jumps in a row restart the guess.
Photo two passed them all: two meters, thirty five thousandths old, ambiguity zero point one, four centimeters from the guess.
